name: RoboFAC Dataset
description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for robotic failure analysis and correction, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset includes six types of failures organized across three hierarchical levels: Task Planning Error, Motion Planning Error, and Execution Control Error.

creator.name: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
creator.affiliation: School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xiamen University; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen

citeAs: Lu, W., Ye, M., Ye, Z., Tao, R., Yang, S., & Zhao, B. (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.12224v3.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset encompasses robotic tasks of varying complexity, ranging from simple short-horizon tasks to complex long-horizon tasks, and tasks executed in dynamic environments. It includes 14 simulated tasks and 6 real-world tasks. The dataset includes six types of failures, spanning three hierarchical levels of error. To account for the diversity of deployment settings in real-world robotics, variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints were introduced.
rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset to increase object diversity and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR to enrich environmental diversity. Real-world data collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Data collection performed via teleoperation with three synchronized viewpoints (wrist-mounted, top-down, and front-left cameras) along with control signals.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data, the original expert policy was replaced with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at the selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. For failures caused by perturbations in the end-effector pose, the perturbed pose was also recorded.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, manual thorough data cleaning was performed and approximately 75% of the collected data was retained.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples corresponding to eight question types: task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction. For each question type, five question templates were provided. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the corresponding textual description. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), both the video and its corresponding textual description were used as inputs to GPT-4o to generate the reference answers.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To ensure annotation quality, all outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Eight question-answer pairs per video trajectory
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was utilized for generating reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction question types.
rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The success rate remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions. The model was trained exclusively on simulation data and six real-world tasks, which may limit generalization to entirely novel manipulation scenarios.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training models capable of Task Understanding, Failure Analysis, and Failure Correction in robotic manipulation. The RoboFAC model can be integrated into a real-world VLA control pipeline as an external supervision providing correction instructions. The training set consists of 60K QA pairs from the simulated RoboFAC dataset. The remaining QA pairs are used for evaluation, including 10K simulated QA pairs and 8K QA pairs from real-world data.
